korea-youth-summit-2027.about:
The Korea Youth Summit is an annual international youth conference organised in Seoul by the Indonesian-based Youth Break the Boundaries (YBB) Foundation. The 2027 edition is themed 'Living Culture, Lasting Legacy' and looks at how tradition and modernity coexist and what role young people play in protecting cultural heritage.

The programme combines panel discussions, workshops, group projects, mentoring and cultural visits in Seoul. It is designed for high school students, university students and young professionals from any country.

There are two routes: self-funded (guaranteed participation without competitive selection, registration open until 5 March 2027) and fully funded (programme fee covered, competitive selection with essays and interview, deadline 20 November 2026). Flights and visas are paid by the participant.
highlights: Fully funded places cover the programme fee
Open to high school and university students worldwide
Panels, workshops and cultural visits in Seoul
korea-youth-summit-2027.eligibility: Young people of any nationality: high school students, university students and young professionals (see the official guidebook for exact age limits). Programme in English.
how_to_apply: Read the guidebook and FAQ on koreayouthsummit.com.
Choose fully funded (essays + interview, by 20 Nov 2026) or self-funded (by 5 Mar 2027).
Create an account and complete the online application; pay the registration fee (USD 10 fully funded / USD 15 self-funded).
Self-funded delegates pay the programme fee in scheduled batches; fully funded candidates complete the interview.
korea-youth-summit-2027.costs: Registration fee USD 10 (fully funded) or USD 15 (self-funded). Self-funded delegates also pay a programme fee in instalments (see the Fees & Payment page). Fully funded: programme fee covered. Flights and visa are your own.

kyoto-icems-internship-program-2027.about:
iCeMS is one of Japan's World Premier International Research Centers, combining cell biology, chemistry, physics and materials science. Every summer its internship programme invites undergraduate students from overseas universities to work in an iCeMS lab.

The programme is aimed at students who want to pursue graduate study at Kyoto University in an iCeMS lab. Applicants must still have at least two semesters of undergraduate study left after the internship.

Details of dates, support and deadline are published in the yearly call on the iCeMS internship page.
highlights: Research at a World Premier International Research Center
For undergraduates at overseas universities
Pathway to graduate school in Kyoto
kyoto-icems-internship-program-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate students at foreign universities with at least two more semesters of study after the programme and interest in graduate school at Kyoto University in an iCeMS lab. Any nationality.
how_to_apply: Check the iCeMS internship page for the 2027 call.
Browse iCeMS labs and pick your preferred hosts.
Prepare transcripts, a statement and recommendation as requested.
Submit before the deadline in the call.
kyoto-icems-internship-program-2027.costs: See the 2027 call for support details.

kyoto-ku-star-india-2027.about:
KU-STAR (Kyoto University Short-Term Academic Research) for India brings undergraduate and master's students from Indian universities to Kyoto for a lab-based internship of about eight weeks in summer (19 May – 10 July in 2026). Interns join a host laboratory from the published list and work on a research project.

It is designed as a recruitment pipeline for Kyoto University doctoral programmes, so applicants should have a genuine interest in a PhD there. International students enrolled at Indian universities are eligible as well as Indian nationals.

Kyoto University provides accommodation for the whole period; in 2026 there was no daily stipend, so travel and living costs were the participant's own.
highlights: Lab internship at one of Asia's top research universities
Free accommodation in Kyoto
Direct pathway to Kyoto University PhD programmes
kyoto-ku-star-india-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates (having completed at least 4 semesters) or master's students currently enrolled at a college or university in India, not graduating before the programme and continuing studies for at least one more semester afterwards. Good academic record and strong interest in a Kyoto University doctorate.
how_to_apply: Read the Application Guide and Host Laboratory List on the KU-STAR India page.
Create an account in the online application system when it opens.
Request a recommendation letter through the system using your Application ID.
Upload all documents and submit before the January deadline. Do not contact labs directly.
kyoto-ku-star-india-2027.costs: Accommodation provided by Kyoto University. In 2026 no stipend; airfare and living costs paid by the participant.

mediterranean-machine-learning-summer-sc.about:
The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School offers a focused five-day programme of keynotes, lectures and practical sessions led by experienced AI researchers from around the world, covering computer vision, natural language processing, generative and diffusion models, reinforcement learning, applied deep learning, neuroscience and ethics. Participants can present their research in poster sessions for early feedback, and social and cultural activities support networking. The 2027 edition takes place in Barcelona, Spain, from 30 August to 3 September.

The school is advertised with a public call and participants are selected on merit. The main audience is doctoral students and exceptional master's students, plus academics and practitioners, from all over the world with a focus on the Mediterranean area. M2L actively promotes diversity through scholarships and outreach.
highlights: Lectures and labs from leading AI researchers
Poster session to present your own research
Scholarships to support diversity
mediterranean-machine-learning-summer-sc.eligibility: Primarily PhD students and exceptional master's students in machine learning or related fields, plus academics and practitioners, from anywhere in the world (focus on the Mediterranean region).
how_to_apply: Watch the M2L website for the 2027 public call
Prepare a CV and a short description of your research or ML experience as requested in the call
Apply online and indicate if you need a scholarship
If selected, register and arrange travel to Barcelona
mediterranean-machine-learning-summer-sc.costs: Registration fee and scholarship details are published with the call. Scholarships are offered to promote diversity; travel and accommodation are usually the participant's responsibility unless covered by a scholarship.

neuromatch-academy-2027.about:
Neuromatch Academy is a global, non-profit online summer school. Its courses are full-time, synchronous programmes held every July: Computational Neuroscience and Deep Learning (5–23 July 2027), and NeuroAI and Computational Behaviour (12–23 July 2027). Participants are matched into pods of 10–15 students with a dedicated teaching assistant by time slot, research interests and language, and spend about 4.5 hours a day on interactive tutorials (Python notebooks) and 3 hours on a group research project with a project TA and mentor.

Courses run in five time slots around the world so students can attend in their daytime, and tuition is globally adjusted to keep the programme accessible. Participants must attend live (no more than two absences for a certificate). Applications for the July 2027 Academy open on 10 February 2027 via the Neuromatch portal.
highlights: Live, pod-based learning with teaching assistants and a real group project
Courses in computational neuroscience, deep learning and NeuroAI
Five time-zone slots and country-adjusted tuition
neuromatch-academy-2027.eligibility: Open worldwide to undergraduate and graduate students, researchers and professionals who meet each course's prerequisites (Python, linear algebra and calculus; NeuroAI requires CompNeuro and Deep Learning or equivalent). Must be able to commit about 8 hours a day for the course weeks.
how_to_apply: Check the prerequisites for your chosen course on the Neuromatch courses page
Create an account on the Neuromatch Academy portal
Apply from 10 February 2027, choosing your course and a daytime time-zone slot
If accepted, pay the country-adjusted tuition (or request any available support) and complete pre-course preparation
neuromatch-academy-2027.costs: Tuition is globally adjusted by country of residence (amounts shown in the application portal). Online, so no travel or housing costs.

osaka-university-science-international-s.about:
The International Summer Program (ISP) places international students in research groups of the Graduate School of Science (mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, earth and space science, macromolecular science) on the Toyonaka campus in Osaka. In 2026 it ran from 16 July to 27 August, with an orientation, a student exchange event and a final presentation.

It is designed for students who are thinking about graduate study in Japan: you join a lab, carry out a small research project and present the results. The 2027 call is expected in December 2026 with a deadline in mid-January 2027.

A limited number of scholarships (about JPY 50,000 or more per month) are offered; the bench fee is waived and tuition (JPY 57,600 in 2026) is waived for students nominated by partner faculties.
highlights: Real research in an Osaka science lab
Scholarships of about JPY 50,000+/month for some participants
Good route into graduate school in Japan
osaka-university-science-international-s.eligibility: Undergraduate or master's students enrolled at a non-Japanese university throughout the programme, with strong interest in natural sciences, GPA above 2.1/3.0, and English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS/TOEIC or equivalent). Open to all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Check the ISP page for the 2027 call (expected December 2026).
Choose three research groups or faculty members you would like to join.
Prepare the application package, a nominator declaration, one recommendation letter, transcript and English test proof.
Submit through the online application system before the deadline (mid-January).
Scholarship results are sent between April and June.
osaka-university-science-international-s.costs: 2026 figures: tuition JPY 57,600 (waived for partner-faculty nominees), bench fee waived, dormitory JPY 20,000–100,000/month, insurance about JPY 1,500. Travel and living costs are your own unless you receive the scholarship.

oxford-machine-learning-school-oxml-2027.about:
The Oxford Machine Learning School (OxML), organised by AI for Global Goals, has trained more than 8,000 learners from 142 countries since 2019. OxML 2027 has three programmes: Foundation Models (June 2027, online only) on how large models are built, trained, evaluated and applied; Biomedical AI (10–12 August 2027) on clinical data, genomics, proteins and molecular design; and Frontier AI (13–15 August 2027). The August programmes can be attended in Oxford with online access, or fully online.

Registration is open now: participants choose individual programmes or a Comprehensive pass for all three, and full-time students can register at a student rate with an academic reference. Lectures are given by researchers from universities and industry labs.
highlights: Lectures by leading ML researchers on foundation models and biomedical AI
Attend in Oxford or online
Student rate with an academic reference
oxford-machine-learning-school-oxml-2027.eligibility: Open to students (undergraduate, master's, PhD), researchers and professionals worldwide with a quantitative or technical background. Student prices require a current academic reference. In-person attendees arrange their own UK visa if needed.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 programme descriptions on the OxML site
Open the registration page and choose Standard or Student registration
Select the Comprehensive pass or individual programmes and online or Oxford format
Enter your details (and academic reference for the student rate) and pay securely online
oxford-machine-learning-school-oxml-2027.costs: Standard prices for 2027: Comprehensive pass GBP 800 online or GBP 1,700 Oxford + online; individual programmes GBP 400 online or GBP 1,100 Oxford + online. Lower student prices with an academic reference. Travel and accommodation not included.

promys-italia-2027.about:
PROMYS Italia, launched in 2025 by the University of Padova's mathematics department with the PROMYS Foundation, follows the Boston PROMYS model: first-year students explore number theory through daily problem sets, lectures and discussions with undergraduate counsellors, guided by the principles of exploration and discovery. Courses are taught in English; the rest of the programme runs in English and Italian. In 2026 it ran 12 July – 22 August in Padova, with places for returning students on more advanced courses.

Applicants must solve a challenging problem set (sent when applications open in January to those who register interest by email) and submit it with a recommendation letter, high-school transcript and an application form with short answers. The 2026 deadline was 5 March, with decisions by 30 April.
highlights: PROMYS-style number theory immersion in a historic university city
Courses taught in English
Real cost of 6,000 EUR subsidised to 3,500 EUR; need-based aid up to full cost
promys-italia-2027.eligibility: Students who by the first day of the programme have completed at least 9th grade (or equivalent), are at least 15 years old, and are not yet full-time university students (the summer before university or a gap year is fine). No nationality restriction is stated.
how_to_apply: Email promys@math.unipd.it to register interest
When applications open (5 January in 2026) you receive the problem set
Write up your solutions and complete the application form with short answers
Send a recommendation letter and your high-school transcript
Submit before the deadline (5 March in 2026); decisions by end of April
promys-italia-2027.costs: Cost in 2026: 3,500 EUR for the six-week residential programme (the real cost of 6,000 EUR is subsidised for every student). Generous need-based financial aid up to the full cost of participation.

riken-international-program-associate-20.about:
The International Program Associate (IPA) programme lets non-Japanese doctoral students carry out their PhD research at RIKEN (Wako, Kobe, Yokohama, Harima and other campuses) under a RIKEN supervisor, through RIKEN's joint graduate school partnerships with universities in Japan and abroad.

Placements usually last one to three years and start in October or April. Applicants first find a RIKEN researcher willing to host them; the researcher contacts RIKEN's personnel office, and the student then applies in the April or September call.

RIKEN covers one round-trip airfare, a living allowance of JPY 5,200 per day, free on-campus housing (or up to JPY 70,000/month rent) and accident insurance.
highlights: Fully funded PhD research at a world-class institute
Housing plus JPY 5,200/day allowance
Calls twice a year (April and September)
riken-international-program-associate-20.eligibility: Non-Japanese PhD students enrolled at a Japanese or overseas university that has (or is signing) a joint graduate school agreement with RIKEN. A RIKEN host researcher must agree to supervise you.
how_to_apply: Browse RIKEN labs and contact a researcher whose work matches yours.
If they agree to host you, they notify RIKEN's Research Personnel Affairs Section.
Apply in the April or September call with the documents requested.
Pass RIKEN screening and internal approval; start in October or April.
riken-international-program-associate-20.costs: Covered: one round-trip airfare, JPY 5,200/day living allowance, free housing or rent up to JPY 70,000/month, accident insurance. No fees.

startmate-accelerator-summer-2027.about:
Startmate is a founder-led accelerator for the Australia and New Zealand ecosystem. The Summer '27 programme runs for 14 weeks from 1 February to 7 May 2027. It is remote-first on Australian time, with in-person weeks for Week 0 in Melbourne, a mid-programme week and Demo Day week.

It is open to any stage, from idea to early revenue, in any industry; solo founders are welcome. Founders can join from anywhere in Australia or New Zealand, or from overseas if they have a strong connection to ANZ, which makes it relevant for international students and graduates of Australian or NZ universities who are building a company.

Each accepted startup receives A$120k at acceptance (A$120k for 8% at a A$1.5m post-money valuation if you have not raised before), plus mentoring from Startmate's network of founders and operators.
highlights: A$120k investment at acceptance, no programme fees
Remote-first: only three in-person weeks
Idea-stage teams accepted; 67% had no revenue when they applied
startmate-accelerator-summer-2027.eligibility: Founders of any age based in Australia or New Zealand, or overseas founders with a strong connection to ANZ. At least one founder must be (or become) full-time. Any industry, any stage.
how_to_apply: Read the accelerator page and FAQs on startmate.com/accelerator.
Create an account on Startmate Universe and complete the online application before 11:59pm AEDT on 1 November 2026.
Shortlisted teams are interviewed; offers go out in mid-December 2026.
Attend Week 0 in Melbourne on 1 February 2027.
startmate-accelerator-summer-2027.costs: No programme fee. Startmate invests A$120k (SAFE or priced round). Travel to the in-person weeks is at your own cost.

startmate-student-founder-bootcamp-2027.about:
The Student Founder Bootcamp is Startmate's entry-level programme for university students who are curious about building a startup. Two editions run in March 2027, one in Sydney and one in Melbourne, each over two days with an overnight stay.

It is open to all university students across Australia and New Zealand, including international students enrolled there, and no prior experience is required. Participants work on ideas with experienced founders and meet other ambitious students; it is a common first step towards Startmate's fellowships and accelerator.
highlights: Two days in person with experienced startup founders
Open to any degree, no experience required
Low fee (A$200) covers accommodation and food
startmate-student-founder-bootcamp-2027.eligibility: Students currently enrolled at a university in Australia or New Zealand (domestic or international). No age limit or prior startup experience required.
how_to_apply: Open the Student Founder Bootcamp page on startmate.com.
Submit the 'Express Interest' form; full applications open in November 2026.
Wait for the outcome, sent shortly after applications close.
Pay the A$200 fee and travel to Sydney or Melbourne in March 2027.
startmate-student-founder-bootcamp-2027.costs: A$200 including GST, covering accommodation and food. Travel to Sydney/Melbourne is at your own cost.

texas-state-honors-summer-math-camp-2027.about:
The Honors Summer Math Camp (HSMC), run by Mathworks at Texas State University in San Marcos, is a full-time, in-person six-week camp for mathematically talented high-school students. First-year campers take an intensive course in number theory and proof-based problem solving alongside other classes and seminars; second- and third-year students work with research mentors on original projects, many of which have won awards in national science competitions.

The 2027 camp runs 20 June – 31 July. Admission is rolling from 1 December until the camp is full, with first acceptances on 15 February. Most campers come from across the US, but students from countries including Albania, Hungary, Bulgaria, Spain, South Korea, Taiwan, China, Indonesia, Mexico and England have attended.
highlights: Six weeks of proof-based number theory with experienced mathematicians
Research projects with mentors for returning students
Scholarships available based on financial need
texas-state-honors-summer-math-camp-2027.eligibility: Mathematically talented high-school students (typically ages 14–18). International students may apply (they arrange their own US visa). A teacher recommendation is required.
how_to_apply: Apply online from 1 December 2026 (rolling admission until full)
Complete the application and ask a teacher for a recommendation
Fill in the financial-needs section if you want a scholarship
Acceptances start 15 February 2027; pay 50% of tuition when you RSVP and the rest three weeks later
texas-state-honors-summer-math-camp-2027.costs: Programme cost USD 6,600 for 2027, covering room, board, books and supplies. Need-based scholarships available. Payments are non-refundable. Travel and visa costs extra.

tohoku-stem-summer-program-tssp-2027.about:
TSSP is Tohoku University's four-week summer programme for freshman and sophomore science and engineering students. It combines lectures on frontier science and technology, disaster science based on the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, hands-on group experiments, and Japanese language and culture. In 2026 it ran from 21 June to 18 July.

Applicants must be full-time undergraduates at a listed partner institution in Australia, Canada, China, Singapore, the UK or the USA, nominated by their home university. Completers receive the equivalent of 8 ECTS credits (transfer decided by the home university).

A JASSO scholarship of JPY 80,000 is available to outstanding students who meet JASSO requirements.
highlights: 8 ECTS-equivalent credits
Disaster science and frontier tech in Sendai
JPY 80,000 JASSO scholarship for eligible students
tohoku-stem-summer-program-tssp-2027.eligibility: Full-time first- or second-year science/engineering undergraduates at Tohoku partner institutions in Australia, Canada, China, Singapore, the UK or the USA, nominated by their home institution.
how_to_apply: Ask your university's international office whether it is a TSSP partner and how it nominates students.
Complete the online registration once it opens (December).
Submit documents before the early-March deadline.
Apply for the JASSO scholarship if eligible.
tohoku-stem-summer-program-tssp-2027.costs: 2026: programme fee JPY 200,000 plus accommodation JPY 189,000 (with breakfast) = JPY 389,000. Travel, other meals and insurance extra. JASSO scholarship JPY 80,000 for eligible students.

ucsc-scholar-immersion-program-2027.about:
The UCSC Scholar Immersion Program (SIP), formerly the Science Internship Program, places high-school students in research projects mentored by University of California, Santa Cruz researchers across the sciences, engineering and other divisions. SIP 2027 is in person, with an online research week (14–17 June), move-in on 20 June and in-person research weeks from 21 June to 6 August, ending in a presentation day. On-campus housing is offered.

Applicants choose from the 2027 research project list and submit transcripts, GPA and one academic reference. Admission decisions are independent of financial need; qualifying scholars receive aid packages covering 25–100% of tuition and programme fees. SIP warns that no third-party agency may charge extra fees: apply only through the official portal.
highlights: Real research in UCSC labs with a university mentor
On-campus housing and a final presentation day
Need-based aid covering 25–100% of costs
ucsc-scholar-immersion-program-2027.eligibility: Students aged 14–17 for the whole programme (some projects require 16+); students who will have graduated high school by summer 2027 are generally ineligible. The page lists no nationality restriction; international applicants must arrange their own travel and US entry documents.
how_to_apply: Join the info session (9 November 2026) and read the SIP 2027 research projects (posted by December 2026)
Apply on the SIP portal between 15 January and 26 February 2027 (noon PST)
Upload unofficial transcripts and GPA; your academic reference is due 5 March 2027
Pay the USD 68 application fee (waivers on request) and optionally submit financial documents
Offers roll out from 9 April 2027; a deposit secures your place
ucsc-scholar-immersion-program-2027.costs: USD 68 application fee (waivers available). Tuition, housing and optional fees are communicated with offers; need-based aid covers 25–100% of tuition and programme fees. Travel extra.

university-of-seoul-international-resear.about:
The UOS International Research Internship places international students in University of Seoul labs for at least 160 hours of research during the 7.5-week summer session (SISS I), earning 3 credits. Labs in engineering, science, urban studies and other fields post their own projects and requirements (some ask for TOEFL 100 or TOPIK 5, a CV and an interview).

The 2026 timeline was: preliminary email application by 27 March, online interviews in early April, results by mid-April, then official summer-session application and payment. The 2027 cycle is expected to follow the same pattern.

The fee includes on-campus housing and cultural field trips, which makes it a practical, structured way to try research in Korea.
highlights: 3 credits for 160+ hours of lab research
Housing and cultural trips included in the fee
Seoul location with semester-long option too
university-of-seoul-international-resear.eligibility: Students from UOS global partner universities (the page also lists a non-partner fee). Each lab sets its own requirements on major and English/Korean level; some positions are for graduate students only.
how_to_apply: Check the OIA International Research Internship page for the 2027 lab list.
Email your preliminary application to uosinternship@uos.ac.kr by the late-March deadline.
Attend an online interview in early April.
If selected, complete the official summer session application and pay via Flywire.
university-of-seoul-international-resear.costs: 2026 fee: KRW 2,400,000 (partner students) or KRW 2,600,000 (non-partners), including on-campus housing and field trips. No stipend.

utokyo-utsip-kashiwa-2027.about:
UTSIP Kashiwa is the Graduate School of Frontier Sciences' summer internship for undergraduate students enrolled at overseas universities. Interns spend the summer in a lab on the Kashiwa campus near Tokyo, in fields such as materials, environmental studies, biosciences, computational biology, ocean technology and complexity science.

It is a way to experience graduate-level research at Japan's top university and to meet potential supervisors for a master's or PhD. The 2026 call closed on 13 January 2026; the 2027 call is expected to open in late 2026 with a similar January deadline.

Support in past cycles has included a scholarship/allowance and help with housing; check the 2027 call for exact amounts.
highlights: Research at the University of Tokyo
Specifically for undergraduates at overseas universities
Strong route into UTokyo graduate admissions
utokyo-utsip-kashiwa-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate students currently enrolled at a university outside Japan, in science or engineering fields relevant to Frontier Sciences labs. Any nationality.
how_to_apply: Watch the Frontier Sciences news page for the UTSIP Kashiwa 2027 announcement (late 2026).
Pick host labs from the list in the call.
Prepare transcripts, a statement of purpose and recommendation as requested.
Submit before the January deadline (17:00 Tokyo time).
utokyo-utsip-kashiwa-2027.costs: Check the 2027 call: past cycles offered support towards living costs; travel is usually at your own cost.
